title: Rust Software Engineer - Rust / C++ (m/f/d)
description:
Quantum Systems develops autonomous, multi-domain systems that operate in the air, on the ground and on the water. Behind every platform is software that has to work reliably in the real world, with limited resources, unreliable connectivity and no second chances.

We are looking for software engineers who like to build exactly that kind of software in Rust and C++. You will join our engineering organization and work on production code that runs on real vehicles and sensors, across a broad range of challenges from low-level systems to scalable services.

We are looking for engineers who quickly understand a complex system and its domain, and who use that understanding to get leverage: designing the architecture, setting the guardrails and guiding several AI agents at once to build, test and iterate faster, while taking full responsibility for the result.

What is your Day to Day Mission:

  • Build and maintain production-grade software in Rust and C++ for autonomous platforms and the systems around them.

  • Design performant, fault-tolerant components that run on embedded Linux, edge hardware and in the cloud.

  • Develop communication layers, data pipelines and real-time processing for sensor-driven, distributed systems.

  • Work with hardware and robotics engineers to get software from simulation and test benches onto real vehicles.

  • Use AI agents as part of your daily engineering workflow: break down problems, run several agents in parallel, review their output critically and make sure it meets our quality and safety standards.

  • Own your code end to end: design, review, testing, deployment and troubleshooting of systems in the field.

  • Shape architecture decisions and help raise engineering standards in a growing team.



What you bring to the team:

  • Several years of professional experience (ideally 4+) building software in Rust and/or C++, including production code.

  • A strong foundation in systems programming: concurrency, memory and resource management, networking and performance tuning.

  • The ability to understand a complex system and its domain quickly, and to translate that understanding into clear architecture and well-scoped tasks.

  • Hands-on experience working with AI coding agents, or the curiosity and drive to build that skill fast, including the judgment to verify and correct what they produce.

  • Day-to-day experience with Linux as a development and target environment.

  • Experience with distributed, real-time or performance-critical systems.

  • A solid testing mindset, from unit tests to hardware-in-the-loop or simulation.

  • Clear communication and the ability to work independently in a fast-moving, interdisciplinary environment.

Nice to have

  • Experience with robotics, autonomy or sensor integration.

  • Experience setting up agent-based workflows, such as parallel agents, automated test and review loops or custom tooling around coding agents.

  • Embedded or real-time experience (RTOS, bare metal, firmware).

  • Familiarity with ROS 2 or simulation frameworks.

  • Knowledge of communication protocols and low-latency data transport.

  • Experience with containers, CI/CD and cloud infrastructure.


Our benefits:

  • Company pension scheme: We support you so that you can already make provisions for later.

  • Flexible working hours: With trust-based working hours, you are not only responsible for your working hours, but also for your work-life balance.

  • Mobile Work: If things get a little busy in the office, you have the option to work remotely one flexible day per week to create the right balance.

  • Stay active: With EGYM Wellpass, you get access to thousands of fitness and sports facilities — and of course, we subsidize the membership.

  • Bike-Leasing: We support you in staying environmentally mobile and healthy.

  • Corporate Benefits: Your opportunity for attractive offers and discounts from well-known suppliers and brands, e.g. Adidas, Apple, Expedia.

  • Employee events: We not only want to grow together, but also celebrate our successes together.

  • Lunch-Card: Be powerful with delicious energy, daily lunch budget is sponsored.

  • Company Shuttle: Enjoy our convenient shuttle service that picks you up from Laim in Munich and brings you to our location, with return trips at the end of the workday.


About us:

Quantum Systems is a leading European deep-tech company for unmanned systems across air, land and maritime domains. We develop and scale integrated hardware, software and AI-powered solutions for mission-critical operations. By combining autonomous platforms with intelligent software and AI, Quantum Systems enables customers to operate, understand and act across domains.


Our commitment:

We are an open-minded company that not only values diversity, but actively promotes it. Regardless of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion, sexual orientation or disability, we firmly believe that the diversity of our employees is an essential part of our success.

At our company, every voice is heard and every perspective is valued. We believe that our differences enrich us and help us to find creative solutions and generate innovative ideas. We pride ourselves on creating an inclusive work environment where all employees can reach their full potential.

An overview of this role

We are looking for a Backend Engineer to join our Change Record team within GitLab’s Source Code stage. As AI agents increasingly write code alongside people, every change needs a clear, trustworthy record of what changed, why, and who or what made it. You’ll build that record into GitLab’s source code experience, for humans and agents alike. That work happens in one of GitLab’s oldest and most complex product areas, where you’ll use Ruby on Rails to improve a critical system serving GitLab.com, self-managed instances, and GitLab Dedicated. Source Code provides the interface layer, through Gitaly, to the Git repositories behind a large share of GitLab traffic, so you’ll help keep it reliable through performance tuning, caching, rate limiting, observability, and resiliency, collaborating with product, design, security, Gitaly, Code Review, and Source Code Experience teams. Supporting production systems and improving established experiences are central to the role, especially while you’re onboarding, and over time you’ll also help build experiences for developers working with agents.

  • Collaborate across functions and teams, both asynchronously and synchronously, and involve domain experts when their input will improve the outcome.
  • Use AI agents for well-scoped work when they can speed up delivery without sacrificing quality, and critically review their output.
  • Write maintainable code that follows GitLab's standards and contribute to constructive code reviews.
  • Help strengthen reliability by monitoring production health metrics, participating in Tier 2 on-call, troubleshooting incidents, contributing to root cause analysis, and improving observability and resiliency.
  • Share knowledge through code review, technical documentation, and everyday collaboration while learning from others.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring

  • Professional experience building backend web applications, services, or application programming interfaces, with experience using Ruby and GraphQL.
  • An understanding of relational databases, structured query language, data modeling, caching, background processing, and backend performance practices.
  • Experience with full-stack development to build and maintain user-facing workflows and their underlying systems.
  • Experience writing backend unit and integration tests, with familiarity with the testing pyramid, Git, and collaborative code review processes.
  • Clear written and spoken English communication skills, including sharing useful status updates in a remote, asynchronous environment.
  • The ability to manage assigned priorities, work through ambiguity, take ownership of your work, and seek guidance when needed.
  • Experience using AI coding agents to speed up software development while critically reviewing their output.
  • Bonus: you’ve built agents or agent-based workflows that run in production, not just prototypes.

The functional team works across Europe and North America, supporting both synchronous and asynchronous collaboration. It includes four engineers, comprising both backend and frontend engineers. We work closely with other Source Code teams, Agentic Preview, Repository Services, and Hardening, as well as other teams in the company such as the Gitaly team, and the AI Governance team.

title: Senior Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

The Trusted Agentic Development team sits within GitLab's Developer Experience group and builds the platforms our engineers rely on every day. GitLab engineers increasingly build software with artificial intelligence agents. Agents can generate code and tests in seconds, but they can also produce passing test suites for software that doesn't work as intended. As a Senior Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development, you'll own the technical thesis for closing that validation gap and build the early proof yourself. You'll rethink what validation means when the author is an agent and make the feedback loop fast, automatic, and trustworthy enough that teams choose to adopt it.

  • Validation that confirms agent-generated code does what was intended, so a passing suite means a working feature and not just a satisfied proxy.
  • Mid-loop feedback that helps an agent self-correct toward working software instead of green assertions.
  • Language-aware approaches under one shared model of what "trusted" means, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, while allowing the right technique to differ by language.
  • Real measurement of whether engineers trust and adopt the path, fed straight back into the platform.

What you’ll do

  • Own the technical thesis for how GitLab validates software when an agent is the author, and turn it into an architecture the team can build against.
  • Prototype the hard parts by building early versions of feedback mechanisms that catch the gap between passing tests and working software, proving what works before the team scales it.
  • Develop approaches for GitLab's primary stacks, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, under one shared definition of "trusted," while allowing the right technique to differ by language.
  • Design the mid-loop feedback an agent needs to self-correct toward working software rather than green assertions, and build the systems that deliver it.
  • Collaborate with engineering teams to adopt these approaches, measure adoption, engineer trust, and validation quality, and use those findings to improve the platform.
  • Set technical direction the team can build on, review designs, and help teammates grow their technical judgment.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring

  • Deep, current, hands-on experience building real software with artificial intelligence agents, ideally across more than one language, and a clear understanding of why agent output can pass tests yet fail in production.
  • A strong point of view on the validation gap and concrete ideas for closing it, backed by approaches you've built or tried.
  • Experience designing distributed systems designed to run on Kubernetes first.
  • The technical range to design systems rather than tune a single framework, and the judgment to know when a solution should be general or language-specific.
  • You prototype to learn, and you ship.
  • The ability to influence engineers across an organization without formal authority through working code and sound reasoning.
  • Strong written communication in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.
  • Alignment with GitLab's values, especially collaboration, iteration, and transparency.

This isn't a quality assurance or test automation role. We aren't looking for depth in a particular testing framework. We're looking for someone who has built with agents, experienced the validation gap firsthand, and wants to solve it.

About the team

The Trusted Agentic Development team is part of GitLab's Developer Experience group. We build platforms and practices that help GitLab engineers validate agent-generated software with confidence. We work across engineering teams and programming languages to understand how people use agents, test new approaches in real workflows, and create a shared model of trusted agentic development that teams choose to adopt.

As a Senior Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic.

The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.

You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.

We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way.

The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time.

What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on.

This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you.

description:

Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

How do we know whether a model is safe - and how do we know whether the systems we built to catch misuse actually catch it?

Anthropic answers both questions with evaluations. We measure model behavior across misuse, prompt injection, and user well-being to inform training and deployment decisions. We also use AI to investigate potential misuse of Claude, analyzing real-world traffic to surface bad actors and emerging threats that drive enforcement actions. Neither is worth much unless the evaluations behind them are representative, robust, and trustworthy.

This role builds the methods and infrastructure that make them so. Sitting at the intersection of applied ML research and engineering, you'll design experiments to improve how we evaluate both model behavior and the agentic systems that govern it, build datasets that represent real abuse rather than clean approximations of it, and ship those methods into the pipelines that gate model training, agent changes, and launch decisions.

Responsibilities

Evaluation research and methodology. Design and run experiments to improve evaluation quality — developing methods to generate representative test data, simulate realistic user behavior, and validate grading accuracy. Research how different factors (multi-turn conversations, tools, long context, user diversity) impact model safety behavior. Analyze evaluation coverage to identify measurement gaps, and evolve evals so they remain unsaturated and high-signal as model and agent capabilities advance.

Agentic investigation evals. Build and own the evaluation harness for an agentic investigation system — defining metrics, test cases, and grading approaches for a complex, long-horizon agent. Measure agent performance end-to-end (detection precision and recall, investigation quality, robustness) and drive hill-climbing on the hardest harm areas. Construct RL environments to improve Claude's safety investigation capabilities.

Datasets grounded in real harm. Construct high-quality eval datasets representing real-world misuse across harm areas such as cyber attacks, bio weapons, and influence operations, drawing from both real traffic patterns and synthetic generation. Collaborate with Policy and Enforcement to translate observed harm patterns into measurable evaluations.

Productionization and tooling. Ship successful research into evaluation, regression, and release pipelines that run during model training, on every agent change, prompt update, and underlying model upgrade, and beyond launch. Build tooling that enables policy experts to author, run, and iterate on evaluations without engineering support. Surface findings to research and training teams to drive upstream model improvements.

  • Experience working with LLMs and a working understanding of their capabilities and failure modes — especially agentic systems with tool use and multi-step reasoning
  • Strong data analysis skills — you can draw reliable insights from large datasets

title: Capacity Engineer
description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations: Austin, Texas

About the role

The Demand Planning team sits at the intersection of traffic forecasting, infrastructure strategy, and operational execution. We predict when, where, and how many servers to deploy across Cloudflare's global edge so that customers' traffic stays in-region and they never have to think about infrastructure. This is not a reporting role — it is a planning and engineering role that requires you to build the models, own the data, and translate forecasts into real deployment decisions.

As a Capacity Engineer, you will own one or more planning regions end-to-end with light supervision. That means maintaining the models, catching problems before they become incidents, working directly with hardware sourcing and infrastructure teams, and contributing to the data pipelines that feed your planning work. You will be the point of contact for your region — not someone who supports a more senior planner, but someone who runs the work.

This is a role for someone with 3-5 years of experience who is ready to operate with real ownership and is actively growing toward full autonomy. You will work alongside senior peers who set team-wide standards, and you will be expected to contribute to cross-regional consistency — not just execute within your own lane. You will also work fluently with AI tooling, including OpenCode AI and MAS agent workflows, as a normal part of how planning gets done on this team.

Why Cloudflare/ Why This Team

Cloudflare's network spans hundreds of cities and carries a meaningful fraction of global internet traffic — the planning decisions this team makes have direct consequences at that scale. The Demand Planning team is in an active transition from manual planning toward intelligent, automated, AI-augmented capacity systems, and this role puts you at the center of that shift. You will work on problems that are genuinely hard, with teammates who take the craft seriously, in a team small enough that your work is visible and your contributions matter from day one.

What you'll do

- Own one or more edge planning regions end-to-end, producing deployment recommendations with minimal supervision

- Maintain and continuously improve regional planning models, incorporating new traffic patterns, hardware generations, and infrastructure changes

- Build and maintain data pipelines that feed regional planning — using BigQuery, Python, and Jupyter notebooks to query, explore, and validate planning data

- Work directly with hardware sourcing, DCS, and infrastructure teams to translate forecasts into actionable deployment plans

- Proactively identify capacity risks in your region and surface them before they require escalation

- Use OpenCode AI and MAS agent tooling as a standard part of your daily planning workflow

- Contribute to cross-regional consistency efforts alongside peers — shared methodology, shared standards

- Participate in planning reviews and communicate forecast outputs clearly to non-technical stakeholders

Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience:

- 3-5 years in an analytical, planning, or technical infrastructure role

- Working SQL proficiency — comfortable querying and joining datasets in BigQuery to answer planning questions

- Python proficiency — data analysis, scripting, and automation of planning workflows; comfortable working in Jupyter notebooks as a day-to-day analysis environment

- Comfort working with large infrastructure datasets and translating them into decisions

- Clear written and verbal communication — you can explain a capacity recommendation to a finance partner or a network engineer without losing either of them

- Demonstrated ability to own a workstream end-to-end with light supervision

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1: We released1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

Please note that applicants who progress to the offer stage of the interview process may be asked to attend an in-person interview within one of the Cloudflare Offices or Cloudflare Hubs. More details about this will be available at that stage of the interview process.

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations. Please note that any offer of employment may be conditioned on your authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export laws without sponsorship for an export license.

The ideal candidate is a "builder" personality with a strong mix of pre-sales/technical customer-facing experience who thrives in an agile, fast-moving environment.
      What you'll do as a Senior Solutions Engineer
      The Pre-Sales Solution Engineering organization owns the technical sales of the Cloudflare solution portfolio, ensuring maximal business value, fit-for-purpose solution design and adoption roadmap for our customers. Solution Engineering is made up of individuals from a wide range of backgrounds including but not limited to Sales Consultants, Technical Consultants, Technical Support and Program Managers.
      You are a customer-facing technologist within the Cloudflare Solutions Engineering team, focused on the developer-first, digital-native segment. You have experience in a pre-sales or other technical customer-facing role, and you're at your best when engaging directly with engineering teams and technical founders. In this role you'll partner closely with the sales team from the very start of the cycle — joining early discovery calls, qualifying opportunities from the get-go, and embedding yourself in customer Slack channels and working sessions. You'll lead technical discovery, deliver compelling demos and architecture discussions, run proof-of-concept builds, and evangelize the Cloudflare Developer Platform as the foundation for our customers' next products and AI initiatives.
      Responsibilities
      Specifically, we are looking for you to:
      • Lead technical discovery within the cloud-developer vertical — asking the right questions to uncover how a customer builds, what they're trying to ship, and where Cloudflare fits.
      • Engage early and often: join sales-led discovery calls from the outset, help qualify deals from the get-go, and stay embedded with customer teams (including in their Slack channels and working sessions) throughout the cycle.
      • Identify and map customer initiatives and business problems — especially around new product development and AI initiatives — to the Cloudflare platform.
      • Build relationships and technical champions within customer accounts, from founding engineers and developers up to the CTO.
      • Develop and present tailored technical content and demos for both hands-on developer audiences and senior technical leadership.
      • Lead demo and proof-of-concept / build activities for Cloudflare prospects and customers.
      • Evangelize the Cloudflare Developer Platform (Workers, Workers AI, Durable Objects, R2, D1, KV, Vectorize, Queues, Pages and more) — making the case for customers to build on Cloudflare, not just use it for storage or CDN.
      • Demonstrate your expertise with your peers through the creation of professional content, including reference architectures, demos, blog posts and other knowledge-sharing activities.
      • Represent and evangelize Cloudflare externally at Developer, Community, Technology and Industry events with thought leadership and expertise.
      • Apply in-depth vertical knowledge or domain expertise. Advise on best practices.
      Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience
      • Previous experience as a Solutions Engineer or other customer-facing technical role, ideally selling to or working with developer-led, cloud-native, or startup organizations.
      • A genuine "builder" mindset and the personality to match: you enjoy talking to developers, you're curious, and you naturally gravitate toward technical problem-solving conversations.
      • The ability to speak engineers' language credibly — you can hold your own on architecture, APIs, and platform design — without this being a hands-on, code-every-day developer role.
      • Strong technical discovery instincts: you know how to draw out requirements, qualify fit early, and separate real needs from noise.
      • A good mix of pre-sales / technical sales experience and comfort operating in an agile, fast-moving environment (joining Slack channels, iterating quickly, engaging in early-stage calls, and qualifying deals from the start).
      • Solid communication, written and presentation skills, with the range to talk to both a hands-on developer and a CTO in the same day.
      • Ability to work on several projects and activities concurrently.
      • Highly driven, curious, team-oriented, and able to work with a sense of urgency.
      • You've built web applications before, or contributed to existing web applications in a meaningful way — enough to have real empathy for how developers work.
      • Polished communication and executive presentation skills with the ability to drive a discussion with a broad range of stakeholders (from the web developer to the CTO/CISO).
      • Relationship building: a proven track record of building deep technical relationships with engineers and technical founders. Experience managing various stakeholder relationships to build consensus on technical solutions/projects.
      • Experience managing technical sales within accounts, including developing champion-style relationships, driving technical wins, and assisting with technical validation.
      • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent in relevant work experience.
      • The role requires up to 50% travel to attend meetings with prospects or customers, attend conferences and other industry events, and to collaborate with your Cloudflare teammates.
      A deep understanding of the Cloudflare Developer Platform and core industry components (and a desire to learn more):
      • The Cloudflare Developer Platform — serverless compute and application development with Workers, Durable Objects, Workers AI, R2, KV, D1, Vectorize, Queues, and Pages. Familiarity with building or architecting applications on a serverless/edge platform is a strong plus.
      • AI/GenAI application patterns — inference at the edge, RAG, vector databases, and how startups are operationalizing AI initiatives.
      • HTTP technologies including reverse proxy (e.g., WAF and CDN), forward proxy (secure web gateway), and serverless application development.
      • Internet security technologies including DDoS and DDoS mitigation, Firewalls, TLS, VPN, DLP.
      • Networking technologies including TCP, UDP, DNS, IPv4 + IPv6, BGP routing, GRE, SD-WAN, MPLS, Global Traffic Management.
      • Zero-trust network access (ZTNA & SASE) concepts including identity management and authentication.
      • Cloud computing technologies such as AWS, GCP, Azure and others.
      • Some scripting or programming familiarity with one or more of JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Golang, BASH — enough to read code, build a demo, and converse with engineers (not to ship production software).
      • Understanding of, or experience with, regulatory requirements such as FedRAMP, GDPR, PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOC-2, ISO/IEC.
      • An undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field. Reminder: this is not a strict requirement at all. Candidates from all walks of life are welcome.
      • You can translate technical concepts and jargon for a wide variety of audiences: from systems engineers, to front-end developers, through to technical founders and C-levels.
      • You want to be constantly learning new things and teaching what you've learned to the broader team through internal and external blog posts, team demos, and product training sessions.
      • You have a knack for understanding problems and finding creative ways to solve them. Our product suite is ever-growing, and knowing how to identify which parts will solve a customer's particular problem is important.
      • You understand how to manage a project, work to deadlines, and prioritize between competing demands.

    • Compensation

      Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location.

    • For San Francisco based hires: Estimated annual salary of $150,000 to $220,000 OTE, Base + Commissions.

    • Equity

      This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan.

title: Customer Engineer, Enterprise - Austin/Dallas,TX or Raleigh, NC

About Us

Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations:

  • Austin, TX
  • Dallas, TX
  • Raleigh, NC

Key Responsibilities

  • Technical Validation: Partner closely with Account Executives to lead technical deep-dive discovery, capture business requirements, and map complex customer infrastructure - DNS, CDN, Zero Trust, Network Security, Workers - to fit-for-purpose Cloudflare architectures and bespoke solutions. . Deliver tailored technical presentations, architectural diagrams, and demonstrations that show how Cloudflare solves specific performance, security, and reliability challenges. Partner with Account Executives to own discovery, demos, onboarding, technical health, risk, and expansion strategy. Proactively monitor customer health scores and telemetry to ensure rapid time-to-value, resolve integration bottlenecks, and reduce deployment risk.
  • Commercial Accountability & Expansion: Carry a variable quota tied directly to new business acquisition and/or ongoing account growth. Be commercially accountable for ensuring deep platform adoption, retaining revenue, and identifying strategic cross-sell and up-sell opportunities based on product usage data. Lead technical Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) to translate platform capabilities into return on investment for C-level executives.
  • Trusted Advisory: Act as a trusted technical advisor throughout the entire customer lifecycle, maintaining a continuous, deep relationship with key stakeholders from initial onboarding through maturity, renewal, and expansion. Provide thought partnership on architecture, AI control layers, security posture, and deployment confidence. Identify potential deployment risks or integration bottlenecks early, and provide remediation strategies to de-risk customer outcomes.
  • AI Orchestration & Workflow Automation: Leverage AI agents, Large Language Models (LLMs), and internal platforms to automate routine tasks such as RFP/Security Questionnaire responses, sandbox provisioning, basic telemetry monitoring, and internal/external documentation, reclaiming your time for strategic customer advisory.
  • Education & Enablement: Partner closely with the Enablement Team to design, build, and govern technical resources. Define, document, and educate both internal teams and customers on deliverables such as Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), architectural best practices, and technical guides to continuously raise the technical baseline across the organization.

  • Experience: Experience in a customer-facing technical role, such as Solutions Engineering, Customer Engineering, Professional Services, Sales Engineering, Technical Account Management, or as a Forward Deployed Engineer (years of experience required will vary based on Associate, Senior, Staff, or Principal leveling).
  • Architectural Mindset: Ability to white-board, design, and articulate complex enterprise network and security architectures clearly.
  • Consultative & Advisory Skills: Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate deeply technical concepts into business outcomes for both hands-on engineers and C-level executives.
  • Commercial Mindset: Proven track record of operating in a quota-carrying or revenue-aligned environment, with a strong understanding of SaaS metrics, business value translation, and enterprise sales cycles.
  • Communication: Exceptional presentation and stakeholder management skills, capable of bridging the gap between deep technical implementation details and high-level C-suite business strategy.
  • Technical Breadth: We do not expect every candidate to be an expert in every domain. Qualified candidates will demonstrate depth in at least four of the technical areas below:
    • Internet fundamentals: Deep understanding of how the Internet works, including OSI Model layers 1–7, BGP, GRE, TCP/UDP, DNS (authoritative and recursive), HTTP(S), and SSL/TLS.
    • Security: Expertise in the security of Internet properties, including WAF, Bot Management, Firewalls, Rate Limiting, (M)TLS, Zero Trust, and SASE concepts.
    • Performance: Expertise in the performance of Internet properties, including speed, latency, caching, video streaming, HTTP/2, and TLS 1.3.
    • AI Proficiency: Familiarity with prompt engineering, AI-assisted scripting and log analysis, LLM utilization, and workflow automation to augment everyday CE workflows.
    • Coding/Scripting: Proficiency in Python, JavaScript, Bash, Lua, Go, or similar languages to write custom integration scripts, API connectors, and edge computing functions.
    • Developer Platform Fluency: Experience designing, building, deploying or scaling applications using RESTful/GraphQL APIs, SDKs, webhooks, and developer tooling in cloud-native environments. Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi), CI/CD pipelines, and observability for developer-led deployments.

title: Customer Reliability Engineer
description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Location: Singapore

Why This Role Exists

Cloudflare built its reputation helping build a better Internet, defending millions of sites, giving away SSL and DDoS mitigation when the industry charged premium prices. In an acceleratingly dangerous world, the scope of that mission has changed. We are becoming something more: critical infrastructure. Banks run their payment rails on us. Governments run public services on us. Media companies depend on us during live events. Health systems depend on us to provide care. Reliability for these customers is no longer a feature of our product. It is a mission.

Serving that customer base demands a different operating model. Traditional support organizations route tickets. Traditional engineering organizations ship features. Neither alone is enough when the stakes are this high. We are pivoting to something different: a customer-facing engineering organization, directly engaged with our customers at scale. This is work a central dev team cannot do from the inside of the network.

The Customer Reliability Engineering function is the spine of that pivot. CRE is SRE applied outward, the same engineering discipline, applied to the reliability of the systems our customers run on Cloudflare. You are the engineer who owns the problems that matter most to the customers who matter most, and you contribute directly to our products and tooling, in partnership with Product Engineering, to hold that standard across the entire customer base.

The Role

CRE is a rapid response team and a proactive engineering team. You fix things at the edge as they come up, and you help build the product capabilities that identify customer issues before they become a crisis. Both modes are equally core.

Rapid response. When a customer issue surfaces that is high-severity, cross-layer and complex, you are the engineer who answers. You reproduce the defect, isolate the root cause across Cloudflare's infrastructure and the customer's stack, drive the fix with Product Engineering, and confirm resolution. You hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global shift rotation.

Proactive engineering. When no fire is burning, you work with Product Engineering and our platform teams to build the capabilities that make the next fire cheaper or unnecessary: telemetry pipelines that correlate signals across the customer base, detectors that fire before a human notices, diagnostic tooling that scales across hundreds of customers, automation that reduces toil for Customer Support. Every incident you carry generates engineering output that reduces the cost of recurrence. The work compounds.

Cloudflare is building CRE as an AI-native function. You will work with and help build agents and tooling that pre-diagnose incidents, surface relevant logs and configuration, and propose fixes with cited evidence. Engineers who ship AI-assisted diagnostics are the ones defining this discipline.

What You Might Work On

Rapid response:

  • Own a Sev-1 incident where a large financial services customer sees asymmetric latency from a single POP. Trace it through BGP routing and origin configuration. Produce the fix upstream.
  • Diagnose a recurring WebSocket disconnect that a media customer has been fighting for weeks. Isolate it to a specific interaction between WAF and their origin load balancer. Drive the fix with Product Engineering.
  • Partner with a government customer's SRE team during an active DDoS event. Help them shape their Magic Transit and WAF configuration in real time.

Proactive engineering:

  • Build, with Product Engineering, a distributed tracing capability that correlates Cloudflare edge signals with customer origin metrics so a single query tells the story of a failing request end-to-end.
  • Ship a detector for a class of WAF false positives silently degrading several customers. Get it into production before the next renewal cycle.
  • Prototype an AI agent that takes a new customer case, pulls relevant logs and config, and proposes a root cause with linked evidence. Deploy it internally. Measure whether it makes engineers faster. Iterate.

Responsibilities

Rapid incident response and root cause analysis. Own the most complex, high-severity customer issues end-to-end, from first signal through confirmed resolution. Lead deep-dive debugging across the full stack: edge, network, DNS, transport, APIs, application, customer-side configuration. Reproduce defects, validate fixes with Engineering, and confirm customer-side resolution. Produce postmortems other engineers rely on. Hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global rotation that includes weekends.

Proactive reliability engineering. Analyze support and telemetry signals across the customer base to find systemic risks before they become incidents. Contribute monitoring, detection, and diagnostic capability to the core product and the engineering systems that give Customer Support early visibility into customer-affecting issues. Define customer-facing reliability metrics (error rates, resolution times, repeat-contact rates) and drive measurable improvement. Write automation that reduces mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-resolve.

Cross-functional partnership. Manage the technical escalation lifecycle with clear ownership and timely communication. Partner with Product Engineering to drive fixes, workarounds, and configuration changes that address underlying gaps. Represent the customer reliability perspective in engineering syncs, incident reviews, and post-mortem processes.

Technical leadership and enablement. Raise the technical floor of Customer Support through pair-debugging, structured knowledge transfer, and shared tooling. Document diagnostic procedures and resolution patterns in runbooks, internal knowledge bases, and AI skills. Share insights from customer-facing incidents to improve product documentation and operational readiness.

Product and platform depth. Maintain deep, current expertise across Cloudflare's product portfolio: edge networking, DNS, CDN, WAF, DDoS mitigation, Zero Trust, Workers, and our developer platform. Anticipate customer impact from new releases and architecture changes. Serve as a go-to subject-matter expert in one or more domains.

Requirements

  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in site reliability engineering, escalation engineering, systems engineering, or a comparable deeply technical support / operations role, with at least 2 years in customer-facing environments.
  • Strong foundation in networking and security:
    • TCP/IP fundamentals: OSI model, IPv4/IPv6 addressing, subnetting, routing, switching.
    • Core protocols: DNS, HTTP/S, TLS/SSL, SMTP, SNMP, NTP.
    • Routing protocols: BGP, OSPF, including path selection and route propagation.
    • Firewall concepts: stateful/stateless inspection, rule sets, NAT, ACLs.
    • VPN and encryption: IPSec, SSL/TLS tunnels, GRE.
    • Zero Trust architecture, network segmentation, modern security models.
  • Proficiency with observability and diagnostic tooling: packet capture and analysis (Wireshark, tcpdump), log aggregation (Kibana, Elasticsearch), metrics dashboards (Grafana), distributed tracing.
  • Strong scripting and automation skills (Bash, Python) with a track record of shipping tooling that improves reliability and reduces toil.
  • Experience with incident management, postmortem culture, and SLO/SLI-based reliability practices.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication. Able to convey complex technical information clearly to engineers, leadership, and customers.
  • Comfort owning ambiguous, cross-layer problems. Composure under pressure during high-severity incidents.

Desired Skills & Experience

  • SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering experience with direct customer-facing accountability.
  • Deep expertise at both L3/L4 (network infrastructure) and L7 (application protocols, DNS, HTTP, WebSocket).
  • Expert-level proficiency with Linux command-line tools: curl, dig, git, traceroute, mtr, strace, ss.
  • Data-at-scale analysis using SQL, PromQL, or equivalent.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi), and container orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker).
  • Track record of building internal tooling or diagnostic utilities that measurably improved team efficiency.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership: mentoring engineers, driving cross-team initiatives, influencing outcomes without direct authority.
  • Experience applying AI/ML to production engineering or operational workflows.
  • Comfort engaging directly with enterprise customer engineering teams, including on calls during incidents.

Bonus Points

  • Active Cloudflare user who understands the platform as a practitioner.
  • Hands-on experience with Workers, Pages, R2, D1, or other developer platform services.
  • Cloud networking and security experience across AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Web programming (HTML, JavaScript) and regular expressions.
  • Chaos engineering or formal reliability frameworks (e.g., Google SRE principles).
  • Managing or configuring non-HTTP services: email, DNS authoritative/recursive, FTP, SSH.

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1: We released1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

We need to make thoughtful infrastructure choices affecting a significant portion of the Internet. Hardware we work with includes GPUs, servers and components, as well as PDUs and network hardware. As a Hardware Systems Engineer, you will work with colleagues on the Engineering teams, Product and Performance teams, and Hardware Sourcing teams to design, qualify and maintain Cloudflare’s worldwide fleet of GPU servers.

What You'll Do

  • Contribute to the technical requirements and end-to-end delivery of AI infrastructure — compute, networking, storage, power, and cooling — not just the accelerator
  • Evaluate, select, and qualify AI hardware platforms (GPUs, custom ASICs, SmartNICs, storage) based on real workload requirements and first-principles analysis
  • Design and validate rack-scale GPU systems: multi-node topologies, high-speed interconnects (NVLink, InfiniBand, RoCE), power distribution, and thermal management
  • Run hands-on qualification: benchmarking, stress testing, failure mode analysis, and vendor RCA — you close the loop yourself
  • Assess and qualify ODM/OEM server platforms; engage directly with vendors and work through the full technical qualification cycle
  • Translate AI product and workload requirements into precise infrastructure specifications
  • Identify gaps in the existing infrastructure stack and drive solutions across hardware, firmware, software, and operations
  • Stay ahead of the AI hardware landscape — new silicon, new interconnects, new form factors — and bring informed, opinionated recommendations
  • Build tooling and automation to support qualification workflows, performance analysis, and ongoing operational visibility
  • Communicate your results and updates through blog posts and internal talks

  • Experience in AI infrastructure, systems engineering, or hardware platform engineering
  • First-principles understanding of AI accelerator architecture: compute pipelines, memory hierarchy (HBM, GDDR), interconnect topology, and/or how workload characteristics map to hardware capabilities
  • Hands-on experience qualifying AI server platforms — you've run NCCL tests, profiled collective operations, debugged NVLink errors, and chased down PCIe lane misconfigurations
  • Understand rack-scale systems: high-density power (kW/rack, busbar, PDU), liquid cooling (rear-door, direct liquid, immersion), high-speed networking infrastructure, and/or physical layer constraints
  • Experience with AI/ML frameworks (vllm, sglang) at the systems level — you understand what they demand from the hardware and where bottlenecks actually live
  • Familiarity with AI server form factors: HGX, OAC, OAM, UBB, open rack standards, and the tradeoffs between them
  • Scripting and automation skills (Python, Bash, Go and Linux sysadmin); you build tooling to support your own work and the team's
  • Strong written communication — you can write a rigorous technical specification and a crisp vendor requirements document
  • Knowledge of performance benchmarking ; Previous experience in testing, measuring, and/or simulating hardware performance and an understanding of no-stone-left-unturned experimentation
  • Knowledge of Redfish, IPMI and server remote management protocols, and experience with firmware updates
  • Harness AI tools and automation to fundamentally accelerate the qualification lifecycle, driving exponential efficiency gains and quality standards.
  • Possess the organizational skills and interest to manage cross-functional technical projects, ensuring architectural designs seamlessly align with delivery schedules.
  • Thrive as a deeply self-motivated engineer in ambiguous environments, demonstrating a strong bias for action and the ability to drive initiatives forward without close supervision.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with major AI server ODMs/OEMs and their qualification and customization processes
  • Exposure to hyperscaler or cloud infrastructure design — understanding how GPU capacity is provisioned, allocated, and operated at scale
  • Experience with RDMA networking, RoCEv2 congestion control, or InfiniBand fabric management
  • Understanding of AI workload patterns: LLM training vs. inference, model/tensor/pipeline parallelism, and their memory and bandwidth implications
  • Familiarity with open compute hardware programs or OCP specifications
  • Experience of performance optimization based on hardware / software codesign
  • Experience of kernel development, compiler optimization, or driver development.
  • Experience of observability and monitoring tools such as Prometheus and Grafana, as well as the ability to observe trends over time
  • Experience with software development tools and processes such as Git, TeamCity and Jira
  • Experience in a hyperscale cloud infrastructure role also valuable
  • Knowledge of debugging server hardware faults and the ability to engage with our sourcing team and vendors to improve quality

Who You Are

  • A self-starter who identifies what needs to be done and executes without waiting to be asked
  • Genuinely curious — you read architecture whitepapers, follow chip announcements, and have opinions on why one memory subsystem beats another
  • Equally comfortable racking servers in a lab and writing a detailed technical requirements document

Sitting within the GTM organization and reporting to a Customer Engineering Senior Leader, you will be responsible for building, coaching, and enabling a high-performing team of quota-carrying technologists. You will ensure your team leverages AI-augmented workflows to eliminate administrative toil and focus on high-value architectural design, technical validation, and the delivery of measurable business outcomes across the entire customer journey.

This is a player-coach role where you have the ability and willingness to step into the field and lead by example. You will manage daily, forecast weekly, and hire always while remaining deeply connected to the technical, commercial, and operational realities of the customer engineering motion.

Key Responsibilities

  • Team Development & Performance: Recruit, onboard, coach, and retain a diverse team of Customer Engineers across multiple levels. Set clear expectations, conduct regular 1:1s and performance reviews, and maintain a strong feedback culture that accelerates growth.
  • Pipeline & Forecasting: Manage your team's opportunity pipeline, forecast new business and expansion outcomes weekly, and own the accuracy of your team's number. Identify risk early and coach reps on deal strategy.
  • Commercial Accountability: Be accountable for your team's achievement of new business acquisition, expansion, adoption, and consumption targets. Partner closely with Sales, Customer Experience, Professional Services, and regional leadership on account planning and execution.
  • Deal Coaching & Technical Strategy: Accompany Customer Engineers on critical customer calls, QBRs, discovery sessions, and PoC reviews. Provide real-time coaching on architecture, commercial positioning, and executive communication.
  • Operational Excellence: Ensure the team operates efficiently within established GTM processes (forecasting, opportunity management, account planning, QBR cadence). Use dashboards and operational reviews to spot trends, unblock friction, and drive consistency.
  • AI & Productivity Enablement: Champion the adoption of AI agents, LLMs, and automation tools across the team. Identify opportunities to reduce toil, improve response quality, and scale technical advisory impact.

Minimum Qualifications

Track record of hiring, developing, and retaining technical talent. Prior quota-carrying Solutions Engineering, Customer Engineering, Sales Engineering, or related technical field experience is strongly preferred.

    • Internet fundamentals: Strong foundational understanding of how the Internet works, including DNS, HTTP(S), TCP/IP, and SSL/TLS.

Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

We are looking for curious and empathetic individuals who are committed to developing themselves and learning new skills, and we are ready to help you do that. We cannot complete our mission without building a diverse and inclusive team. We hire the best people based on an evaluation of their potential and support them throughout their time at Cloudflare. Come join us!

About the Department

Cloudflare’s engineering teams build and maintain the systems and products that power our global platform. A global platform which is within approximately 50 milliseconds of about 95% of the Internet connected population, serving on average, over 46 million HTTP requests per second.

About the Team

Delivering this platform with high performance and efficiency depends on advanced Linux kernel and hardware capabilities, and that is where this team works.

The Performance Team owns overall system and application performance across that fleet: resource optimization, instrumentation, and the tooling that lets us see what the hardware is actually doing. System memory sits alongside CPU cycles, network processing, and storage IOPS as a first-class resource, and how the kernel manages it is increasingly the thing that decides how hot we can safely run every machine we own.

We work upstream first. Several of us maintain or regularly contribute to the Linux kernel, and our default is to fix problems in mainline rather than carry private patches. This role is built on that principle.

The problem you would own

Using memory efficiently is one of the highest-leverage problems we have. At our scale, how the kernel's memory-management subsystem behaves under pressure has direct consequences for both performance and cost. As DRAM prices climb, getting more out of the memory we already own is a real lever on infrastructure spend.

Using custom low-overhead instrumentation on production servers, we have identified several scalability bottlenecks in the kernel memory layer that show up under real workloads. We are looking for an expert to take on these problems, fix them against production workloads, and drive the changes upstream.   • Land your work upstream. We expect MM changes to go to mainline first and want you to keep doing the maintainership and review work that earns standing in the community.
  • Build and extend low-overhead kernel instrumentation (tracepoints, BPF, perf) so we keep measuring before we change, and prove the impact afterwards.
  • Partner with kernel, networking, storage, and product engineers across the company to turn observed system behavior into concrete MM improvements.
  • Set technical direction for how Cloudflare uses, tunes, and evolves kernel memory management as we push utilization higher.

Requirements

  • Deep expertise in the Linux kernel memory-management subsystem: the page allocator, virtual memory and memory mapping, reclaim, and the locking and concurrency that hold it together.
  • A track record of upstream Linux contribution, ideally including maintainership or sustained work in MM or an adjacent subsystem.
  • Strong systems programming in C, with the judgement to make high-risk changes to shared infrastructure safely.
  • Ability to dive deep into a complex codebase while keeping the fleet-wide picture in mind, and to own a problem and its outcome rather than a single patch.
  • Clear communication with engineers across many teams, since the symptoms of an MM problem usually show up far from the MM code.

Bonuses

  • Strong understanding of Linux kernel internals pertaining to memory management
  • Experience troubleshooting and resolving performance issues in large-scale distributed systems.
  • Experience with large scale configuration/deployment management.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

About the Department

Cloudforce One is Cloudflare's threat operations and research team, responsible for identifying and disrupting cyber threats ranging from sophisticated cyber criminal activity to nation-state sponsored advanced persistent threats (APTs). Cloudforce One works in close partnership with external organizations and internal Cloudflare teams, continuously developing operational tradecraft and expanding ever-growing sources of threat intelligence to enable expedited threat hunting and remediation.

Members of Cloudforce One are at the helm of leveraging an incredibly vast and varied set of data points that only one of the world's largest global networks can provide. The team analyzes these unique data points at massive scale and efficiency, synthesizing findings into actionable threat intelligence to better protect our customers.

About INTERDICT

I.N.T.E.R.D.I.C.T. (Identify, Neutralize, Triage, Engage, Respond, Disrupt, Integrate, Contain, Threat Hunting) is Cloudforce One's unified operational security organization responsible for identifying, analyzing, and responding to threats targeting Cloudflare and its customers. INTERDICT encompasses three main sub-functions:

  • PhishGuard: Email Managed Detection and Response (MDR) service.
  • Cloudflare Managed Defense (CMD, Formerly SOCaaS): 24/7 monitoring, detection, and mitigation of security events across Cloudflare products.
  • Detection Engineering: Develops, maintains, and deploys Cloudflare’s threat detection logic across email, application, and network telemetry.

Through the combined capabilities of CMD, PhishGuard, and Detection Engineering, INTERDICT delivers a cohesive operational security function that provides continuous, proactive protection against network, application, and email-based threats. This integrated structure ensures rapid detection, coordinated response, and improved security outcomes for Cloudflare and its customers.

About the Role

The Response Engineer within the Cloudflare Managed Defense Center acts as a primary technical responder for Cloudflare's premium enterprise customers. You will autonomously investigate complex threat telemetry, handle live incident response for sophisticated volumetric DDoS and application-layer attacks, and analyze traffic anomalies during high-pressure events.

Customers contact the Managed Defense Center for assistance and intelligence across Cloudflare's security portfolio, focused on two core pillars: Web Application Security (WAF and Bot Management) and DDoS mitigation across network and application layers.

Managed Defense Response Engineers use customer-facing dashboards and internal tools to make detailed and informed suggestions for mitigation, and may implement mitigation strategies directly on behalf of the customer. The team provides continuous proactive monitoring and analysis of security events through internal alerting systems.

We are looking for an analytical security practitioner who thrives in this always-on operational environment and bridges the gap between deep technical analysis and premium customer advisory.

Role Responsibilities

  • Implement robust mitigation strategies for complex attacks across OSI Layers 3, 4, and 7 using Cloudflare's suite (Magic Transit, Magic Firewall, Advanced TCP Protection, Advanced DNS Protection, WAF, Custom Rules, IP Access Rules, Bot Management, and Rate Limiting)
  • Monitor and investigate proactive alerts, performing near real-time packet and traffic flow analysis and correlation to detect protocol exhaustion and application-layer exploitation, translating findings into custom, highly targeted mitigation rules
  • Review alerts to determine relevancy and urgency, proactively escalate customer-impacting incidents, and adhere to Customer SLAs for alert response and customer communication
  • Act as the primary technical contact for customers during active security incidents, driving high-touch, consultative communication (via phone, chat, email) with customers' technical engineering teams to neutralize threats while ensuring stable traffic delivery
  • Continuously tune and optimize existing security monitoring rules and alerting thresholds to improve the operational signal-to-noise ratio and reduce false positives
  • Lead managed customer onboarding sessions, maintain customer-specific runbooks, and deliver highly technical monthly security posture reviews and post-incident reports
  • Partner directly with internal engineering, product, and threat intelligence teams to provide actionable feedback on attack trends, tooling gaps, and product enhancements

Role Requirements

  • 4–7 years of direct, hands-on experience in Managed Detection and Response (MDR), advanced Security Operations, or high-level Technical Support/Incident Response for enterprise infrastructure
  • Proven capability to handle both Application Security (including knowledge of OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, L7 WAF, HTTP/S anomalies, Bot mitigation) and Network Security (L3/L4 volumetric DDoS, protocol abuse)
  • Working knowledge of threat frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK to classify adversary behavior and inform detection and mitigation strategies
  • Operational understanding of internet protocols including TCP, UDP, ICMP, GRE, BGP, DNS, with the ability to quickly diagnose attack fingerprints and infrastructure impact during volumetric DDoS attacks

Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations

  • San Francisco, US
  • We are only considering locally based candidates OR candidates looking to move to the Bay Area.

  • Senior Customer Engineer - (AI & Start-Ups)

    • For San Francisco based hires: Estimated annual salary of $213,500 – $335,500 OTE, Base + Commissions.

Your superpower is technical discovery, translation, and evangelism: understanding what a builder is trying to accomplish, mapping it to the full breadth of the Cloudflare Developer Platform, and inspiring teams to build on Cloudflare rather than just consume a single service.
